Flu Outbreak Disrupts Canadian Electric Utilities Workforce, Atco Ltd/Canada Among Firms Hit

An influenza outbreak sweeping through several Canadian provinces has disrupted operations across the electric utilities sector, according to industry officials and union representatives. The illness, which began affecting employees late last week, has resulted in staff shortages at power generation plants and maintenance sites, causing delays in scheduled maintenance and periodic outages in some regions.

Atco Ltd/Canada confirmed Tuesday that more than 60 of its field workers in Alberta and Saskatchewan are currently on sick leave due to the flu, prompting the company to postpone certain non-essential upgrades. “Our primary concern is the well-being of our employees and the continued delivery of reliable power,” said Atco Ltd/Canada spokesperson Lila Fernandez. “We are actively monitoring the situation and redeploying staff where possible to maintain critical operations.”

The Canadian Electrical Utilities Association reported that at least five major operators, including Atco Ltd/Canada and Prairie Grid Energy, have been forced to operate with reduced crews. According to the association, some rural substations have experienced short-term service interruptions as companies struggle to fill shifts. “There have been pockets of service disruptions, mostly in smaller communities,” said association president Marc Gagnon. “We’re working with health authorities to contain the outbreak and support affected staff.”

The Power Workers’ Union estimates that up to 12% of front-line utility staff in affected areas are currently absent. Union president Shelley Grant warned that continued high absenteeism could further strain the grid, especially if cold weather increases demand. “We urge all companies to prioritize worker health and limit overtime to prevent burnout,” Grant said.

As the outbreak continues, utilities are urging customers to report outages promptly and conserve electricity where possible. Health officials have advised affected companies to step up disinfection protocols and encourage vaccination among staff.
